english_verification.review_scope: Representative current-Mod country definition, formation decision and mission range read; fixed-revision Khozrugan Wiki stub read for ruler, Rugan Orc, Great Dookan and Venomtooth genealogy. The stub does not certify complete history, current mechanics or a unique predecessor; no exhaustive mission or national-idea audit. Native English idea names/descriptions were compared by localisation key with the current Mod. Wide line ranges locate separately read passages, not exhaustive coverage. No formal validator, build, browser or gameplay test was run.

rationale.campaign_length: 36 missions expand the conquest across all Cannor.
rationale.colonization: No confirmed route is centred on overseas colonization.
rationale.complexity: Formation, the duel and subject management require preparation, but there is no high-frequency complex dedicated interface.
rationale.dark_story: The main line centres on Greentide revival, burning and conquest of an empire, making the overall narrative distinctly dark.
rationale.difficulty: It is powerful in individual wars; the real difficulties are aggressive expansion, coring and economic tempo.
rationale.diplomacy: Clan subjects are useful, but diplomacy mainly serves war and subject management.
rationale.early_pressure: Before formation you depend on the starting Orc; after formation you must handle the duel, subjects and expansion preparation.
rationale.magic_artifice_intensity: No dedicated system centred on everyday magic or artificery is confirmed.
rationale.narrative_density: Greentide inheritance and the Cannor-conquest goal are clear, but the current mission structure advances mainly through consecutive territorial objectives.
rationale.tall_play: Both formation and the mission line demand wide expansion; development is not the core loop.
rationale.trade_economy: The economy mainly funds armies and coring; trade is not the narrative focus.
rationale.warfare: Ideas, mission rewards and end-state goals almost all serve continuous continental war.

identity.appearance: Eligible green or grey Orcs can form Khozrugan through the Reorganize the Western Army decision; Unguldavor- or Grombar-related events can also release it or change a Tag to it.

national_ideas.scope_note: National traditions, seven national ideas and ambition only; optional idea groups and racial/government bonuses are excluded. Conditional alternatives are separate, not stacked. Accepting new ideas on formation depends on the actual event/decision and player choice.

description.text:
Urak Dul!

Once the warcry that broke kingdoms and peoples roared across these lands. But, after the bitter losses of Rottenstep and Castonath and the inglorious defeat of the Greentide, the battlefield no longer quakes with the bellows of orcish valor. Instead a festering doubt has taken hold in the minds of warriors, shamans, and chieftains alike. Was it a mistake to war against the humans? Was the Dookanson wrong?

Hah! These are the ponderings of weak-willed maggots! Are they true orcs? Or are they mewling warg pups? The past belongs to the forgotten. The present belongs to the living. And the future belongs only to those who will seize it.

description.text: The living memory of the Greentide has all but faded away. And the times before, when our forebears roamed the caverns and tunnels of the Serpentspine, are nothing more than stories passed down. Yet there are those who still hold onto these bygone relics. Stubborn shamans who insist we “keep with the old ways”. Zealous fanatics who decry those of us who acknowledge Corin’s strength or look inward toward the orcish soul. Pithering fools all of them and soon to be tongueless. Tradition is the corpse of wisdom. Let it be buried alongside the rest of the dead.

description.text:
“Built long ago, when the human empire of Castanor still stood, Bal Mire was built to watch over wild Alenic tribes. By the time of Khozrugan, the fabled fortress had fallen into disrepair and ruin, sinking into the swampy mud that it was built atop.

Its settlement as the capital of the newly formed Khozrugan and its refounding as Ur Morduba was amongst the boldest decisions made by the orcish state, for the orcs had focused on the wholesale destruction of fortresses rather than restoration. It proved a wise decision when the war with the adventuring companies of Cobalt Company and Brave Brothers began. Many an adventurer would see their demise in the swampy surrounds…”

- Khozrugan: A Legacy of the Greentide by Armyn Stynài, Chapter 2

description.text:
To this day, even after generations, there are many amongst us who fail to recognize what the greatest spoil of victory is - land. It is the land that grows the foodstuffs that feed our clans. It is the land that supports the livestock our wargs feast on. It is the land that bears us the iron we need most for further conquests. But, the land does not offer this freely. Hands are needed to till, herd, and mine. Hands that are not always willing to provide as they should.

No matter, for we shall declare Osulband, the earthbinding. Those who are too weak to fight, shall be forever tied to the land. It is the finest honor we could ever grant, for they shall be the ones to tend to our greatest spoil.

description.text:
“Tazhor-u Bazu, or demonstration of strength, is as old as the worship of Dookan himself. Before their arrival in Escann, during the more fractious days of the Serpentspine, the sport varied greatly across the clans. All forms of it involved some level of wrestling within a marked arena, but which moves were allowed or even what constituted victory was rarely defined.

While some standardization would occur within the unified Greentide, its core rules would not be settled until the founding of Khozrugan. Due its focus on dominance, victory would center around the submission of the opponent via grapples and takedowns with old tactics such as biting and punching being discouraged and eventually banned. Eventually the ruleset became popular to see adoption in Unguldavor and even distant Bramund.”

- Khozrugan: A Legacy of the Greentide by Armyn Stynài, Chapter 7

description.text:
“Oi, you slacking off? Think you can get away with being lazy because I’m a halfling anbakh? Hey, where’d your smile go? Reminded me a lot of my predecessor’s ugly mug. Know what happened to him? No? Simple, I broke his skull in. Moment I caught him stealing from the crop, I tackled him down and smashed him til that smile was no more. Got to take his place soon after. No questions asked.

You see, Warchief’s got no tolerance for filth like that. And neither do I. So best you shape if you want to keep that smile of yours…”

-Daroosh Bloodfirst to an orcish farmhand

description.text:
“Known as the Anbahk in orcish, the Overseers gradually came to as the labors of Osulband began to bear fruit. The loot and communal loyalty that once held the chieftains and clans’ the Khozrguan hierarchy collapsed giving rise to plantation retinues and serfs rather than warriors and clansmen rose.

While the arrangement was more akin to that of the era of Feudalistic Cannor than the rising centralized states of Age of Unraveling, it did enable the orcish state to quickly establish an administration that could support its expansionist tendencies and desires.”

- Khozrugan: A Legacy of the Greentide by Armyn Stynài, Chapter 11

player_overview.avoid_if: If you want peaceful development, trade colonization, complex diplomacy, magic mechanics or many story branches, Khozrugan will feel repetitive.
player_overview.how_it_plays: Prepare Feudalism, Administrative Technology and a qualified ruler before formation; afterward rely on strong infantry and subjects for a continuing western conquest while digesting new territory, aggressive expansion and administrative-point pressure.
player_overview.overview: Khozrugan is a conquest state formed when green or grey Orcs reorganize the Western Army. It has no elaborate interface system, instead combining strong infantry, clan subjects, a founding duel and successive claims into a direct and effective war machine; the real enemy is often aggressive expansion, coring costs and an ever-longer conquest list rather than the battlefield.
player_overview.recommended_for: Players who enjoy strong armies, continuous wars, map painting and a clear continental endpoint.
signature_features: After formation, the Ostokhan duel resolves the crisis of rule, and victory can permanently strengthen the army.
Three high-opinion clan subjects provide extra troops and multi-front capacity early on.
The missions move from unifying West Castanor to dismantling Anbennar and conquering and unifying Cannor.
player_overview.tagline: Relight the Greentide and roll across West Cannor with Orc armies until all Cannor submits.

reasons: The Orcish formable identity, Ostokhan duel and clan subjects create a clear founding phase.
Infantry strength and military rewards suit continuous conquest.
The campaign has a clear long-term objective from West Castanor to a unified Cannor.
It suits players who enjoy map painting, army management and an expansion snowball.
warnings: Aggressive expansion, coring costs, administrative points and the economy are harder to manage than any single war.
The mission narrative is a straight conquest line with relatively little peaceful-development content or branching events.
It is not an independent 1444 starting country; the pre-formation experience depends on the chosen Orc country.
The offline Wiki country page is short; rulers, culture, religion and Venomtooth genealogy were supplemented, but the complete prehistory remains incomplete.

values.rationale: The evidence clearly establishes extreme conquest, military obedience and a society of strength, but does not provide equally strong evidence for slavery, sacrifice, genocide or treating population as a resource. War and continental unification are not counted as evidence of evil by themselves.
